long_biography.plain_text:
A 1996 investment in a ship-repair yard in Rostov-on-Don linked Vadim Vikulov's freight business to agricultural exports. The port geography created access to grain markets. He moved from brokering tanker charters and trading oil products into handling, processing and selling crops across the Azov–Black Sea basin.

Aston subsequently assembled a connected food-and-export network. Its assets now cover grain storage, oilseed processing, vegetable-oil production, marine terminals and freight operations, while the company supplies food ingredients in Russia and overseas. Vikulov combined ownership with long-term operating control, serving successively as board chairman, president and chief executive while the group expanded its production and logistics base.
